How I choose priorities and track progress

Only your moves in fully analyzed, saved games count. Select “I played White” or “I played Black”, or let me detect EarthsDirtiest. Example games and practice completions do not raise your game score. Reanalyzing a match or correcting your side replaces its report.

The score starts at 100. An evaluation loss of at least half a pawn costs points for that move: a one-pawn loss costs 20, capped at 60. Allowing or losing a found forced mate costs 70 separately, without pretending mate is a pawn value. Those penalties are averaged over your moves. A move matching the previous engine choice is not penalized for a changed follow-up search.

Priorities combine error frequency and severity across your latest 10 analyzed games, with recent games weighted more strongly. Tactical labels require legal board evidence; unexplained losses become calculation practice. Progress compares equal groups of up to five unique reviews in analysis order. Different opponents, positions and search settings can affect the scores.

Opening and tactic recommendations teach relevant habits using the available prepared exercises. Earlier saved games contribute after you reopen and fully analyze them.
